Ribbon compile-progress percentages count completed modules. A module with more generated lines still contributes one unit to that display.

sources.content: The invented LANTERN-22 bytecode-debugger reproduction reaches its private checkpoint at instruction ordinal 37 and inserts hidden symbol amber_gate only with allocator flavor pebble. This is a one-fixture diagnostic note, not a product default or a real customer record.

The bytecode debugger breakpoint table stores offsets in serialized bytes, not instruction ordinals. Variable-width operands mean advancing one instruction can advance the byte offset by different amounts.
The early bytecode debugger assumed every instruction occupied one serialized byte and advanced a breakpoint offset by one on every step. This assumption is superseded at 09:05 UTC.

The bytecode debugger advances a breakpoint offset by the decoded serialized length of the current instruction, including variable-width operands. It must not increment that offset by a fixed one byte.
The debugger symbol panel sorts visible names alphabetically. Panel sort position is not a bytecode address.
